attributes.body_ja:
「だって」は、助動詞（じょどうし）の「だ」と副助詞（ふくじょし）「とて」（「と」＋「て」）からできている表現（ひょうげん）で、会話（かいわ）で使（つか）われることが多（おお）いです。使（つか）い方（かた）はいろいろありますが、基本的（きほんてき）には、前（まえ）に述（の）べられたことに、話（はな）し手（て）が主張（しゅちょう）を加（くわ）えるときに使（つか）われます。「だって」は、文（ぶん）のどこで使（つか）われるかによって、「なぜなら」「～と聞（き）いた（伝聞（でんぶん））」「でも」など、意味（いみ）が変（か）わります。

文（ぶん）の始（はじ）まりの「だって」は、主（おも）に話（はな）し手（て）が前（まえ）に述（の）べられた内容（ないよう）に不満（ふまん）を持（も）っていて、それに反対（はんたい）の意見（いけん）を述（の）べたり、理由（りゆう）を伝（つた）えたりするときに使（つか）われます。この「だって」は、「でも」や「なぜなら」に似（に）ています。

文（ぶん）の終（お）わりの「だって」は、伝聞（でんぶん）を表（あらわ）します。この「だって」には、「なん」が付（つ）きます。「なんだって」は名詞（めいし）のあとや「の」や「こと」で名詞化（めいしか）された文（ぶん）のあとで使（つか）われます。

注意点（ちゅういてん）

名詞（めいし）の直後（ちょくご）に置（お）かれた「だって」は、「でも」と似（に）た意味（いみ）で使（つか）われて、「(A) も同（おな）じこと」や「(A) も例外（れいがい）ではない」ことを表（あらわ）します。この「だって」の前（まえ）には、「なん」は付（つ）きません。

豆知識（まめちしき）

副助詞（ふくじょし）の「とて」は、「と⾔（い）って」や「と思（おも）って」を短（みじか）くしたものです。「だとて」という言（い）い方（かた）もありますが、「だって」の方（ほう）が言（い）いやすいので、ふつうは「だって」が使（つか）われます。

豆知識（まめちしき）

「だって」から始（はじ）まる文（ぶん）では、その終（お）わりに「もん」や「もの」が付（つ）くことがあります。これは、話（はな）し手（て）が理由（りゆう）を強（つよ）く伝（つた）えるときの言（い）い方（かた）です。自分（じぶん）は悪（わる）くないというニュアンスで、主（おも）に女性（じょせい）や子（こ）どもが使（つか）います。

  • 私（わたし）もそんなもの食（た）べたくないよ。だって、不味（まず）いもん。
    I also don't want to eat something like that. It's because it tastes bad.
  • 今日（きょう）は家（いえ）から出（で）ません。だって、今日（きょう）は暑（あつ）いもの。
    I am not going to leave my house today. Cause it is hot today.
attributes.body:
だって is a colloquial combination of the auxiliary verb だ, and the adverbial particle とて in Japanese (a combination of the particles と, and て). It has a wide range of uses, but primarily exclaims that something is the 'premise' for whatever has been said, or will be said next. This 'exclamation' is usually translated as 'I heard', 'cause', 'but', or 'even if'. The meaning that will be conveyed is determined primarily by where だって appears in a sentence.

When placed at the beginning of a sentence, だって highlights the speaker's (usually) displeasure about something that has just been said, before following it with an explanation or counterpoint. This だって is quite similar to でも.

At the end of a sentence, だって is used to express hearsay, in a similar way to 'I heard that', or 'it was said that', in English. In these cases it will be preceded by なん. なんだって always appears after a noun, or a phrase that has been nominalized (with の or こと).

Caution

When used directly after a noun, だって has a similar nuance to the だって that appears at the beginning of sentences (emphasizing what has come before it, in order to explain further). This comes across as でも, and may not be used with なん.

Fun Fact

The adverbial particle とて itself is an abbreviation of expressions like と言（い）って, and と思（おも）って. だとて (the full construction) may also be used, but is almost always replaced by だって, as it is far easier to say.

Fun Fact

When used at the beginning of a sentence, もん or もの will often come at the end of that sentence, in order to strengthen the opinion given by the speaker. This is more commonly used by women and children.

  • 私（わたし）もそんなもの食（た）べたくないよ。だって、不味（まず）いもん。
    I also don't want to eat something like that. It's because it tastes bad.
  • 今日（きょう）は家（いえ）から出（で）ません。だって、今日（きょう）は暑（あつ）いもの。
    I am not going to leave my house today. Cause it is hot today.

attributes.source: [AIAIJ] An Integrated Approach to Intermediate Japanese

attributes.description: Using 「って」 or 「て」 for 「という」

attributes.body: だって and それでも both express contradiction. だって is casual and often used at the start of a sentence to offer an objection, e.g., だって疲れたもん ('But I'm tired!'). それでも is less casual and shows contrast with a neutral tone, e.g., 雨だった。それでも行った ('It was rainy, but I still went.').

first_relatable.meaning: I heard/was said, Because, But, Even or also, Even if or even though

second_relatable.title: それでも
second_relatable.meaning: But still, And yet, Even so, Nevertheless

attributes.body: Both expressions involve だって, but their usage differs. んだって appears at the end of a sentence and means 'I hear (A)' or 'they say (A)', with an explanatory nuance added by ん. In contrast, だって is more flexible. It can appear at the beginning, middle, or end of a sentence, and has several meanings. It can function as a casual 'because', 'even though', or 'they say (A)', depending on context.

first_relatable.title: んだって
first_relatable.meaning: I heard that, He or She said that

second_relatable.title: だって
second_relatable.meaning: I heard/was said, Because, But, Even or also, Even if or even though

attributes.body: These are two expressions that can look very similar, or even identical in some cases, as たって when used with nouns will become だって. As an overall guideline, だって is a casual expression used to express 'I hear (A)' or 'they say (A)', or as a colloquial 'because', while たって is one way to say 'even though (A)' or 'even (A)', similar to ても or でも.

first_relatable.title: だって
first_relatable.meaning: I heard/was said, Because, But, Even or also, Even if or even though

second_relatable.title: たって
second_relatable.meaning: Even if, Even though, No matter how

attributes.body: Both can be used to report hearsay (i.e. 'they say (A)'), but differ in tone and nuance. ということだ is more formal and can carry the nuance of summarizing or confidently reporting what the speaker heard. だって is much more casual and light, and can also be used at the beginning of a sentence with an emphatic 'but I mean (A)' nuance, which is something ということだ cannot do.

first_relatable.title: ということだ
first_relatable.meaning: I heard that, Rumor has it that, It is said that, It means that

second_relatable.title: だって
second_relatable.meaning: I heard/was said, Because, But, Even or also, Even if or even though

attributes.body: Both can be used to express reasons, but だって is highly casual, colloquial, and emotional, while なぜなら〜から is formal and objective-sounding. Also, なぜなら〜から begins a sentence, and clearly introduces a reason for something just stated, while だって can be used in sentence-final position. Depending on usage, だって can also have the meanings of 'I hear' and 'even though', which なぜなら〜から does not have.

first_relatable.title: だって
first_relatable.meaning: I heard/was said, Because, But, Even or also, Even if or even though

second_relatable.title: なぜなら〜から
second_relatable.meaning: Because, The reason is, That is because

attributes.body: Both ときいた and だって express hearsay, but differ in tone and formality. ときいた means 'I heard that (A)' and is neutral and conveys information directly heard by the speaker, while だって is casual and emphatic, often used in conversation to mean something like 'They say (A).' or 'I'm telling you (A).'.
